thread.title: Town of Turtle Board delays decision on cost agreement with data center developer - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Town of Turtle Board delays decision on cost agreement with data center developer - NewsBreak

author: KYLIE BALK-YAATENEN
title: Town of Turtle Board delays decision on cost agreement with data center developer - NewsBreak
text:
By KYLIE BALK-YAATENEN ,
7 hours ago
TURTLE— After almost an hour of public comment a and gnarly 30 minutes of board discussion, Turtle town supervisors decided to hold off for a month deciding on a cost reimbursement agreement with Panattoni on a potential data center project.
The town board indicated it had an agreement largely ironed out, but supervisors Chris Walsh, Tim Kopp and Town Chairman Roger Anclam all agreed they want more information on what the reimbursement pay would cover.
Town of Turtle attorney Michael Davis said it's not fully clear what the money would cover. Davis said he knows it would pay some amount for consultants like himself and any professionals. But it's not clear if it would pay fully for research, studies and other work a data center proposal would require.
Walsh said town officials, including the fire chief, want more information about data centers. She suggested a payback agreement should cover travel, food and lodging tied to trips town officials might take to research communities that have data centers.
Walsh said she bets the fire department is not properly trained to handle data center fires, which can involve batteries that burn at a high temperature. She wants more information on whether the reimbursement agreement could cover extra training for fire crews.
The cost reimbursement
In a cost reimbursement between the town and Panattoni, town officials would require the developer to cover the cost of outside consultants and professional services tied to the project.
A town memo laying out a proposed agreement with Panattoni Development Co. explains the developer would provide the Town of Turtle with an initial $250,000 deposit. It would pay for town costs linked to review of development applications and project plans.
According to the agreement, the town could use the funds to hire outside attorneys, engineers, accountants and other specialized consultants needed to vet the proposal. The agreement specifically excludes charges for time spent by town employees working on the project.
The developer would receive monthly invoices detailing town expenses. If the balance of the deposit fell below $50,000, the developer would be required to deposit an additional $50,000 within 10 business days.
The agreement would not grant or guarantee any formal approval for the prospective data center. It states any project-related applications would require review and approval by the Town of Turtle Plan Commission and town board.
In addition to covering review costs, the agreement includes provisions addressing public records, conflicts of interest, compliance with anti-corruption laws and indemnification of the town against certain legal claims related to the project.
The document also provides the town with a perpetual license to use studies, reports and other work products funded through the developer’s deposits for municipal planning, regulatory and public purposes, even if the agreement is terminated.
The agreement requires the developer to notify the town of any litigation, governmental investigations, bankruptcy proceedings or changes in company control that could affect the project.
Panattoni, a company based in Irvine, California, has taken over for Meta and Cambrin in the Towns of Beloit and Turtle. Panattoni says on its website it brings more than 40 years of experience delivering large-scale industrial and technology projects.
It says the company’s approach “emphasizes collaboration, transparency and long-term community engagement.”
The proposed town of Beloit data center would be a 430-acre, 700,000-square-foot, hyperscale data center campus. It would be situated on an aging rock quarry off South Prairie Avenue.
Panattoni does not say on a frequently asked questions page on its website whether the town of Turtle portion of the project would increase the scope or size of the data center proposed.
The company only says that “a potential new, large-scale data center campus is being considered in (the Towns of) Beloit and Turtle to support the growing demand for digital infrastructure."
Opposition
Over 100 people filled Turtle Town Hall Wednesday night to speak out against the data center prospect, with some calling for an 18-month moratorium on data centers.
The overflow crowd was large enough that people had to stand in the back. Some brought lawn chairs to sit.
Everyone who spoke voiced opposition to Panattoni's plans.
Lauren Walsh, a town resident, wants more information on the plan, and she thinks the community has a right to know where board members are getting their information.
She suggested billion-dollar corporations' research contains biased information. Walsh said the town needs more time to think things through.
“Large corporations like that do not make decisions about what time is on our side. We can take the time we need to give the amount of thought and consideration to any decision, especially one this large, and we deserve to do this for our community,” she said. “Their emergency does not need to be our emergency.”
Denise Vandefleet shared worries a data center could affect tourism in a state that promotes rivers, lakes, wide-open green spaces and other environmental resources.
“Let's preserve undeveloped, non-urban spaces for the air, the trees, the peace, fish, wildlife, and for the people, the residents of this community,” she said.
Some people said they worry a data center could change the landscape and threaten wildlife and farmland preservation.
Sue Fugate directly called out Town Chairman Roger Anclam, claiming Anclam had been vague about when he signed a nondisclosure agreement for the data center prospect.
She pressed him to tell her. Anclam said he signed it in the fall of 2025.
